data.description:
## Description
**What**: Build a synthetic diff fixture with three planted violations -- (a) a new test with no header, (b) a new test asserting only on mock.called_with(...), (c) a new test whose intent_id claims a slug but whose only assertion is `assert True == True` -- alongside an unmodified legacy test block, run /dso:review against it, and assert the resulting reviewer-findings.json contains Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings located inside cases (a)(b)(c) and zero such findings inside the unmodified legacy block.
**Why**: Validates that the SC4 dimensions have both recall (fire on real violations) and precision (do not fire on exempt legacy code), closing the loop on the enforcement path.
**Scope**:
- IN: The synthetic fixture diff; the /dso:review run; assertion on findings[] dimension and source_path:source_line placement for the three violations and the legacy block.
- OUT: The reviewer dimension definitions (draft-3); rule text (draft-1).

## Done Definitions

- a /dso:review run against the synthetic 3-case diff produces a reviewer-findings.json containing at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 finding whose source_path:source_line falls inside violation (a) ← Satisfies: sc-5
- the same reviewer-findings.json contains at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 finding inside violation (b) and at least one inside violation (c) ← Satisfies: sc-5
- the same reviewer-findings.json contains zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings whose source_line falls inside any unmodified legacy test block in the diff ← Satisfies: sc-5
- the tests written for this story carry valid Rule 6 headers ← Satisfies: sc-5
- unit tests written and passing assert the fixture-review output placement of findings across the three violations and the legacy block ← Satisfies: sc-5

## Considerations

- [Observability] The claim-vs-assertion contradiction check (case c) degrades semantically until the 94ed-f55c manifest ships; the fixture should use a slug-format intent_id consistent with the published manifest schema.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, I want a synthetic 3-case review fixture proving the test-quality dimensions fire on planted violations and stay silent on legacy blocks, so reviewer precision is demonstrated
